_comment: SkillSpector suppressions for this repo, passed to the scanner with --baseline by
dev-review's scripts/skill-scan.mjs. Discipline lives in skill-maintainer's
references/standards.md: an entry is added only on the operator's word, is scoped as
narrowly as its cause with a LITERAL matcher, and its reason carries a 'Still flag
Adjudicated finding by finding in issue 62. Three sections:
rules[]       - findings the scanner reports, suppressed by literal id+path
coverage[]    - files the scanner could not finish reading. NOT a finding, and
the scanner's own baseline cannot express it; this section is
read by our guard only. Accepting one does not accept another:
a skill still blocks if any unread file is unaccounted for.

rules.reason: conventions.md documents the workflow's own comment protocol - the '<!-- vsk:v1 type=... -->' marker every artifact opens with - so a scanner looking for instructions hidden in HTML comments matches the documentation of the mechanism, not an instance of it. The markers are metadata read by guard scripts, carry no imperative, and the file is shared by ten skills, which is why one cause produces ten findings. Still flag if: a marker example gains text addressed to the agent rather than key=value metadata, or the pattern appears in a file that is not documenting the protocol.

The brief template shows the same '<!-- vsk:v1 type=brief ... -->' marker an issue body must open with, inside a fenced markdown block that a reader copies. It is an example of the protocol above, in the one file whose job is to show it. Still flag if: the template's HTML comments gain prose addressed to the agent rather than key=value metadata.

The template opens with '<!-- vsk-dev:start -->', the delimiter dev-setup uses to find and re-render the one block of AGENTS.md it owns. It is a machine-readable boundary marker, deliberately invisible in rendered markdown, and dev-setup would be unable to edit idempotently without it. Still flag if: the delimiter comment gains content beyond the marker itself, or a second unexplained comment appears in the template.

harness-facts.md documents how each harness discovers skills, including Claude Code's '@path/to/file' import syntax and the HTML-comment source citations ('<!-- source: CLAUDE-CODE-SKILLS -->') that tie every normative sentence to the page it came from. A scanner reading a file that explains agent-file mechanics will match the mechanics being explained. Still flag if: a citation comment stops naming a source and starts containing instructions, or an import example is written as something to execute rather than to recognise.

standards.md carries the same '<!-- source: ... -->' citation comments, which are how a reader tells a verified normative sentence from commentary and how the weekly refresh knows which sentences a drifted source invalidates. Removing them would make the freshness contract unauditable. Still flag if: a source comment carries anything but a source identifier, or an uncited HTML comment appears among the normative sentences.

authoring.md marks the tables it mirrors from skill-maintainer's standards with '<!-- mirrored -->' so the refresh runner knows which copies must move together. It is a synchronisation marker between two files, not an instruction. Still flag if: a mirrored marker gains prose, or the comment appears on content that is not actually mirrored elsewhere.

Every refresh contract carries HTML comments naming which reference sections a drifted source invalidates - the mapping the refresh runner reads to build its PR. It is machine-readable bookkeeping about this repo's own files. Scope of what this hides, stated plainly: the path matches the refresh contract of ALL twelve skills, while only three report the finding today; a hidden instruction added to any skill's REFRESH.md would be silenced by this rule. It is written this way because the contracts share one authored format and one purpose, and per-skill rules would drift apart. Still flag if: a comment in a refresh contract addresses the agent directly rather than naming an affected file or section.

fingerprints.reason: skillify only. RA1 (Rogue Agent / self-modification) is CORRECT about the pattern and is accepted with its limits stated, not explained away: this refresh contract instructs an agent to rewrite skillify's own marked sections when upstream sources drift. What actually bounds it, verified: refresh work runs on refresh/** branches, and .github/workflows/refresh-guard.yml fails any such PR whose diff touches anything outside a skill's refresh/ directory - so the automated path cannot reach skillify's SKILL.md or references at all. Checksums, versions and timestamps in refresh/sources.json are runner-only by repo rule, and the workflow maintains one standing PR rather than pushing. What bounds it as of 01-09-2026: the default branch IS branch-protected - a PR is required, force-pushes and deletion are blocked, and admins are not exempt - so 'a human reviews before merge' is now an enforced control rather than a convention. This sentence previously recorded the opposite, and the protection was enabled because this suppression depended on a control that did not exist. Still narrower than it sounds: refresh-guard only constrains refresh/** branches, so an agent following this contract from any other branch is bounded by the PR requirement alone. The residual risk is therefore real but not unique to this contract: it is the same risk carried by any agent with write access to the repository, and the finding is accepted on that basis rather than on a control that does not exist. Still flag if: this contract's wording changes at all (content-hashed, so it re-triggers automatically), or refresh-guard.yml stops restricting refresh/** diffs to refresh/ directories - that guard is the one real bound named here.

coverage.reason: The scanner reports static_parse_limit on this file and degrades 1 static analyzer(s) for the whole skill. What is established: the degradation is the scanner's bounded shell parser giving up, not a property of this file's behaviour - a control experiment isolated one trigger, a JavaScript template literal in assignment position, which degrades a two-line file while forty template literals inside function calls do not degrade at all. What is NOT established: that this is the trigger in this particular file. The specific span was not isolated per file, and this acceptance does not claim it was. It is accepted because the alternative is banning ordinary syntax from every skill that ships a script, and because the acceptance is bound to this file's exact contents - any edit drops it and forces re-adjudication. Still flag if: the reported reason code changes from static_parse_limit, or the number of degraded analyzers rises above 1 - either means a cause other than the one accepted here.

Accepts the eight AE1 findings on this file. AE1 is a completeness signal reported through the findings channel - the scanner's own text is 'Referenced artifact was not completely inspected' - so it is accepted here rather than as a rule or fingerprint. Two traced causes: this SKILL.md cites repo-root paths (packages/cli/packaging.json, packages/cli/scripts/validate-skill.mjs, CONTRIBUTING.md, .vegastack/dev.md) that cannot resolve relative to a skill directory and are correct for a skill whose subject is this repository; and it links to references/standards.md, which the parser cannot finish for the reason on that file's own entry. Not a rule, because {id: AE1, path: SKILL.md} silences this in all twelve skills and demonstrably hid a real regression when tried. Not fingerprints, because the scanner emits eight location-bound hashes while its own generator deduplicates them to two, so a fingerprint set provably cannot cover them. Scope of what this hides: any AE1 on this one file. Still flag if: this file changes at all - the sha256 above drops the acceptance automatically - or a rule id other than AE1 appears here, which this acceptance does not cover and which will still block.
